changes.reason: This finding targets ep_ajax_priv_wp_ajax_wcf_upload_checkout_file (the authenticated hook at checkout-ajax.php:57) but claims auth_required:none. WordPress fires wp_ajax_ hooks only for authenticated users; unauthenticated calls are routed to wp_ajax_nopriv_ hooks. The core vulnerability claim — missing capability check in upload_checkout_file() — is real (confirmed in source) but already covered by agent-a2-f22-upload-checkout-file with the same code references. This finding's auth claim is factually wrong for the named entry point, and its severity rating of 'critical' is not warranted for media-only uploads (master allowlist at helper.php:1934 restricts to jpg/jpeg/png/gif/webp/ico/pdf/mp3/m4a/wav/mp4/m4v/mov; PHP is blocked).

The finding contains two material evidence errors: (1) the claimed sink line 325 is not wp_handle_upload — line 325 is wp_send_json_error() for a blocked file type; wp_handle_upload is called at line 425 inside move_uploaded_file(); (2) the PoC uses the wrong file field name 'wcf_upload_file' — the actual field is 'wcf_checkout_file' (checkout-ajax.php:301, :311). Additionally, the claim that .html, .svg, and .xml files can be uploaded is false: the master allowlist at classes/class-cartflows-helper.php:1934 restricts to jpg/jpeg/png/gif/webp/ico/pdf/mp3/m4a/wav/mp4/m4v/mov. The underlying observation (no capability check on the nopriv handler) is correct but already fully addressed by cartflows-a1-001 with accurate code references.
